report:
The unchanged whole-original P19.2 completion criterion is not settled. The manuscript establishes substantial mathematical obstructions for its explicitly defined signatures, but it does not establish that equation (22) is necessary for the original programme or that its model category exhausts the originally permitted approximations. There is also an unverified extension from smooth to arbitrary normal model total spaces.

I checked the entire candidate, including its appendix. The author’s provenance record and earlier verdicts supply no evidence. R is used as caller-granted mathematics: “Only the ENTIRE accepted original P19.1 bodyR is a mathematical grant, in its exact smooth fixed compact-Kahler class, prescribed-start and usual Gauss-carrier scope.” Its applications to the constructed ray have the prescribed smooth manifold, fixed Kähler class, start zero, squared-log time, usual supported carrier and probability entropy. R supplies maximalization, divisorial determination, maximal-ray energy and the nonmaximal entropy classification; it supplies no identification of the original P19.2 approximation signature.

The scope problem is substantive. The original text requires preservation of all required energy, entropy and singularity data, distinguishes I from P data, and also identifies regularization of log-discrepancy-model rays as a residual goal. It does not explicitly require simultaneous recovery of the usual datum, its NA energy and every interior Legendre P-level raw mass for every arbitrary weak ray. Distinguishing P-equivalence from I-equivalence does not itself prescribe pointwise raw-mass convergence. Freezing a signature makes a theorem precise; it does not prove that this signature is mandatory for the unchanged task. Energy is particularly consequential here: the constructed ray has analytic radial energy −c₀/2 and usual NA energy zero. Equation (22) chooses recovery of the latter. The original programme’s intended energy requirement must be identified before these alternatives can be equated. The target is neither usual maximal nor I-maximal, so it does not refute a regularization statement restricted to log-discrepancy-model/I-maximal rays. Likewise, the original text does not establish that every permitted noncanonical weight must have a bounded compatible extension. The manuscript expressly excludes weights carrying additional nonmodel singularities. These are unresolved identifications, rather than a demonstrated mathematical counterexample to every interpretation of P19.2.

The lower-rooftop and positive-mass closedness arguments check out. A competitor for the I-envelope of a finite lower roof is a competitor for each constituent ceiling, so it lies below the roof. This proves I-model closedness without global sections. The DDNL mixed-mass estimate supplies a common positive mass bound for a dS-convergent sequence with positive-mass limit. Theorem 5.6 then supplies genuine lower rooftop tails, with positive mass after deleting an initial segment. Its proof controls finite roofs by the volume diamond inequality and summable mass errors. Decreasing closure makes these tails I-model; increasing closure at the positive-mass P-model limit finishes the argument. The distinction between DDNL’s C-ceiling and P-ceiling is harmless here because every relevant limiting application has positive mass. Consequently the stronger dS obstruction is established for all usual-datum maximal finite-energy rays from zero, including genuine cutoff levels.

Both maximality comparison directions are valid in the smooth compact-Kähler setting. The local Gauss calculation uses normal-coordinate weight divided by ord_F(τ), with generic divisorial coefficients. A potential independent of τ contributes its generic normal coefficient multiplied by that normal weight; −λ log|τ|² contributes −λ ord_F(τ). The locally bounded-above supremum rule then gives (10). Countable reduction permits simultaneous generic points for the coefficients; pullback and usc regularization agree as psh functions because they agree off the exceptional set. This requires no polarization. I-maximization preserves the ideals and hence these coefficients, raises level masses and retains finite energy. R’s maximality and Legendre injectivity therefore identify a usual maximal ray with its I-maximization.

For the converse, each coefficient profile f is finite, nonnegative, nondecreasing and convex. The zero-infimum argument correctly works on every fixed modification: monotone pullbacks converge almost everywhere off the exceptional locus, hence locally in L1; upper semicontinuity of point Lelong numbers forces the divisorial coefficients to decrease to zero. Equation (23) gives the positive conjugate parameters through rational rescaling of valuations. The conjugate is finite and continuous for q>0. Positive supporting slopes are recovered by rational approximation; a zero supporting slope forces f(λ)=0, and the stated bounds imply g(q)→0 as q↓0. Thus (24) recovers both profiles. Point blowups recover point Lelong numbers on every projective analytic modification, and the valuative ideal criterion gives I-equivalence. Equal normalized I-ceilings then give equality of levels and rays. This reconstruction does not use MP Section 5.2 or projective density.

The Cantor construction is sound. Cylinder masses tend to zero, giving atomlessness, while 2^(−m)log(4r_m²) tends to −∞ at every point of K. The Green potential is locally finite outside K and globally L1, so its pole set is exactly K. The compact atomlessness argument gives the required uniform small-ball control. Jensen and Fubini prove exponential integrability for every fixed exponent, including neighborhoods meeting K. Consequently all multiplier ideals of ch are trivial. The current is (1−c)ω_C+cν; its nonpluripolar part discards precisely cν and has mass 1−c. Positive-mass envelope preservation and idempotence justify q_c, whose I-envelope is zero.

The torus and product arguments also check out. Each nonzero integral alternating form defines a proper closed analytic condition on the connected space of oriented complex structures; Baire avoidance gives a two-torus with no nonzero integral (1,1) class. Its constant Hermitian form is Kähler. Restriction to this factor proves both nonprojectivity of X and that [ω] is not proportional to a line-bundle class. Fiberwise restriction proves the finite product rooftop identity before taking its increasing envelope limit. Truncation and the vanishing of two curve factors give M_k(Q_c)=1−kc/3. The pole set has zero smooth area, so the smooth background contribution loses no mass.

The complete test curve, including its endpoints, is legitimate. Its raw extended values are concave and usc even on K. P-maximization preserves the interior masses. The decreasing endpoint limit dominates q_c₀ and has the same positive mass; the relative full-mass characterization identifies their P-ceilings. The relative Legendre theorem produces an actual finite-energy weak ray. The available −1 level and nonpositive ceilings give −t≤U_t≤0, including uniform convergence and therefore strong convergence to zero at the start. Its energy is exactly E(U_t)=−tc₀/2 by affinity and the test-curve formula. All genuine levels have trivial ideals; the local Gauss formula gives zero on divisorial points, and R gives zero on the full supported carrier. The maximal ray of this datum is stationary. Thus U is nonmaximal, H(U_0)=0, and R gives entropy slope +∞.

The compatible-weight lemma is correct under its stated comparison antecedent: both actual weights must have the same vertical divisor and bounded residual extensions near the central fiber and the initial boundary. A finite central cover and one compact joining annulus produce one all-time bound for each pair. Taking infima in time preserves placeholders and gives bounded Legendre differences. P-ceilings, raw mixed masses and usual data agree; energy monotonicity gives identical slopes. Canonical nef/obstacle rays are correctly included through usual maximality, without asserting bounded extensions. Actual finite-energy I-maximal flag rays are included through the proved converse. No formal nonpositive ideal is turned into an actual approximant merely by assertion.

However, Section 1 defines cohomological models using normal total spaces, whereas MP Lemma 5.1.8 and SD Lemma 4.6 explicitly assume smooth dominating total spaces. Their stated results validate the smooth relatively Kähler branch. Resolving a normal model does not automatically preserve relative Kähler positivity of the unchanged pulled-back class. The manuscript supplies neither a normal-space compatible Perron theorem nor a proof that the needed bounded extension and usual maximality survive this passage with the same divisor. Premise 11 therefore remains unverified. Its evidence passages record the source/grant boundaries, rather than establish the asserted normal extension. The compatible-weight argument remains valid whenever its bounded-extension antecedent is actually established.

Equations (25)–(26) give a valid all-sequence obstruction for the verified category. The cutoff b_j is the actual trivial-valuation value by (10); c_j is the NA energy and analytic slope of the replacing usual maximal ray by R. Legendre energy gives b_j−c_j=∫_(−∞)^(b_j)(1−M_n)dλ. Deficits are measurable and nonnegative by mass monotonicity, and the integral is finite by finite energy. Allowed bounded replacements preserve the actual P-level masses. Since b_j→0, every fixed interval (−1,−ε) eventually lies below the cutoff. Pointwise recovery and Fatou then give 0≥c₀(1−ε)²/2>0. This uses no dS convergence, analytic-energy recovery of the target, uniform level convergence or finite-time entropy hypothesis.

The established signature is precisely recovery of φ_j(v_triv), E_α(φ_j), and pointwise fixed-volume-normalized raw top masses of closed P-level ceilings on (−1,0). The established categories are all usual maximal finite-energy rays from zero, actual I-maximal finite-energy rays, and actual compatible subgeodesics for which comparison with a canonical maximal ray has the required bounded extensions. Smooth relatively Kähler models and canonical usual-maximal nef/obstacle rays are included. Separately, the dS obstruction requires only one positive-mass target level and usual maximal approximants. Neither result currently establishes the unchanged whole-original conclusion.

Harmless wording corrections: “bounded ray” should read “bounded at every finite time”; dS on unrestricted singularity types is a pseudometric, becoming nondegenerate on the positive-mass normalized model ceilings used here; and on a normal model D needs the real Cartier/cohomological meaning required to define compatibility. Extending the normal-model theorem or proving the original signature/category identification requires additional arguments, not wording changes.

premises: DX Theorem 2.13: On a compact Kähler manifold with a smooth pseudoeffective form θ, two θ-psh potentials have identical multiplier ideals at every positive coefficient if and only if their pullbacks have identical point Lelong numbers on every smooth projective analytic modification.

DX Proposition 2.18: For a θ-psh potential on a compact Kähler manifold with smooth pseudoeffective θ, its I-envelope is admissible, I-equivalent to the potential, P-model, and dominates its P-envelope; consequently the I-envelope is idempotent.

DX Lemma 2.21: In the same setting, a genuine decreasing limit of I-model P-model potentials is I-model when the limit is P-model; an increasing almost-everywhere limit is I-model when the limit is P-model of positive nonpluripolar top mass.

DX Lemma 3.14: For a nonempty locally uniformly bounded-above family of psh functions on a complex manifold, the point Lelong number of its usc supremum equals the infimum of the constituent point Lelong numbers.

Darvas–Di Nezza–Lu, Monotonicity, Theorem 1.1: On a compact Kähler n-fold, for smooth closed real forms θ_j and θ_j-psh potentials u_j,v_j, if each u_j is less singular than v_j, then the integrated nonpluripolar mixed product of the u_j is at least that of the v_j.

Darvas–Di Nezza–Lu, Monotonicity, Theorems 3.12 and 3.14, and DDNL Section 2: In a big class, P[u] preserves nonpluripolar top mass and is idempotent at positive mass. For a reference φ of positive mass and u more singular than φ, relative full mass is equivalent to P[u]=P[φ].

DDNL Lemmas 3.4 and 3.7: In a Kähler class of volume V, ordered singularity types satisfy dS/V=(n+1)^(−1)Σ_k(M_k(v)−M_k(u)), where M_k is the fixed-volume-normalized mixed mass. Each mixed-mass difference is bounded in absolute value by C dS/V for arbitrary types.

DDNL Corollary 4.7 and Proposition 4.8: A genuine decreasing limit of normalized model ceilings is a model ceiling; if their top masses have a common positive lower bound, all mixed masses converge to those of the limit. Positive-mass C-ceilings equal P-ceilings.

DDNL Theorem 5.6 and its proof: A dS-convergent sequence of normalized P-model potentials with common positive top-mass lower bound and positive-mass P-model limit has a subsequence whose lower rooftop tails increase almost everywhere to the limit. After an initial deletion, the finite roofs and tails are genuine P-models of positive mass.

DXZ Theorem 2.6, specialized to a compact Kähler manifold with Kähler form ω and reference zero: Closed Legendre duality identifies maximal test curves with weak geodesic rays from zero. Finite energy is equivalent to finiteness of the integrated mass deficit, and the radial energy is b+∫_(−∞)^b(M_n(χ_λ)−1)dλ, with cutoff b and fixed-volume normalization.

DXZ Section 2.2: On a compact Kähler manifold in a big class, a relative test curve with positive-mass limiting reference can be maximized by applying P to interior levels and taking the decreasing left limit at the cutoff. Applying P_I instead gives an I-maximal relative test curve with reference P_I of the original reference.

For a smooth compact Kähler manifold and a dominating equivariant normal compact Kähler test configuration with real vertical Cartier divisor D and relatively Kähler class α_X+D, its canonical Perron weak ray from smooth zero is usual-datum maximal and has a locally bounded residual extension after removing D near the central fiber and the finite-time initial boundary.
